body:
> Observed 2026-08-28 on hkb's own board, three times in three minutes. `hkb request-changes` on #146 (22:35:38), #150 (22:37:20) and #148 (22:38:26) set each card to `ready`, as the protocol says (`review --request-changes--→ ready (same branch)`). Within 13–15 s each was back in `review`: the next tick — the Actions dispatcher on the `issues` event; the laptop loop's log shows no reconcile line — hit the `active_pr` guard (`src/dispatch.js` ~704: a `ready` card with an open PR → `review`). Label timeline of #150: `ready` labeled 22:37:20, unlabeled 22:37:32, `review` labeled 22:37:33. No worker was ever relaunched; the review sits on the card and nothing reads it.

## Why

Two rules in the protocol contradict each other for exactly the card `request-changes` produces. The guard exists so a card whose PR is open is never claimed a second time — right for a worker that finished and is waiting on review. But `request-changes` *means* "the PR is open and must be continued": its whole output is a `ready` card with an open PR. On any board with a dispatcher the verb is therefore a no-op — the reviewer's brief lands in the attempt history, the card bounces back to `review`, and the loop the protocol draws (`review → ready → running → review`) never turns. Reviewers today have to close the PR (losing the branch's context for the next attempt) or merge `main` and fix by hand. `protocol.md:64` even says *"PR state never gates readiness"* — the guard is the one place it does.

There is a second half. Even with the guard fixed, the next attempt gets a fresh `kb-<n>-<k+1>` checkout on a fresh `worktree-kb-<n>-<k+1>` branch, and its brief says *"work only in this worktree, on the current branch"* — so it would open a **second** PR for the same card. The review does reach it (the `changes_requested` attempt row is rendered in `hkb context`), but nothing tells it which PR and branch to continue.

## What

1. **The guard honours `changes_requested`** (`src/dispatch.js` claim loop, pure predicate in `src/model.js`): a `ready` card whose latest attempt row is `changes_requested` (synthetic `reviewer` row, `protocol.md:39`) is **claimable** despite its open PR — that PR is the continuation target, not a duplicate risk. Every other open-PR case keeps the guard. The predicate takes the attempts and the PR list, so the test is a table.
2. **The next attempt continues the PR.** In `src/dispatch.js`/`src/board.js` where the worktree is made for a claim: when the card's latest attempt is `changes_requested` and it has an open PR, create the worktree **from the PR's head branch** (`kb-<n>-<k+1>` checkout, branch = the PR's `headRefName`, fetched first) instead of from the default branch — for the `claude --bg` / `claude -p` profiles that means passing the branch to the harness's worktree flag or creating the worktree with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` before the launch (the dispatcher already does this for Codex, `docs/harnesses.md`). If the harness's flag cannot take an existing branch, fall back to a fresh worktree plus an explicit instruction (item 3) — say which path was taken in the attempt row (`continues_pr: <number>`).
3. **The brief says so** (`src/context.js`): a card with a `changes_requested` latest attempt and an open PR gets one block near the top — *"PR #147 (branch `worktree-kb-146-1`) is open with changes requested — see attempt 2 below. Continue that PR: work on its branch, merge `origin/<default>` into it first, push (never force), and finish with `hkb finish` — do not open a second PR."* — and the generic "on the current branch" line is adjusted when item 2 checked that branch out.
4. **`hkb finish` on a continued PR** already moves the card to `review` (open PR → review); make sure the result comment names the PR it continued rather than "opened". `hkb request-changes` prints the next step in its one-liner: `#146 → ready (PR #147 stays open; the next attempt continues it)`.
5. **Docs**: `protocol.md` state table and the tick's guard list (`active_pr` → review *unless the latest attempt is changes_requested*), and line 64's claim; `README` review section; the wiki page covering the dispatcher/guards (`node .repolore/scripts/wiki-check.mjs`).

## Done when

- On a board with a running dispatcher, `hkb request-changes <n> "…"` on a `review` card with an open PR results, within two ticks, in a `running` attempt k+1 whose checkout is on the PR's branch (or whose brief names the PR to continue), and the PR count for the card stays at one after that attempt finishes.
- A `ready` card with an open PR and **no** `changes_requested` row is still guarded to `review` (table test both ways).
- `hkb log <n>` reads `review_requested → changes_requested → completed` across the same PR.
- `npm run lint && npm test` green (dispatch fake-gh test for the claim, context test for the block); `npm run smoke` if the brief text changed.

## Contract

- Do not drop the guard for the ordinary case; the exemption is keyed on the synthetic reviewer row only.
- Never `git push --force` anywhere in this; continuing the branch means merging main into it.
- Touches the claim loop in `src/dispatch.js` beside #143/#144/#150 — keep the change local to the guard and worktree creation.
goal: hkb request-changes produces a card the dispatcher actually relaunches, on the same PR: the active_pr guard exempts a card whose latest attempt is changes_requested, the next attempt works on the PR branch, and the brief names the PR to continue
title: request-changes is undone by the active_pr guard on the next tick, and the next attempt would open a second PR
